fichas.title: Insulated glazing: construction and pane-surface numbering
fichas.summary: Insulated glazing consists of two or three panes. Pane combinations, coatings, and the sealed space between panes influence its specific properties. Coatings are numbered by pane-surface position; the diagrams identify positions 1–6 and show outside and inside orientation.

fichas.title: Thermally insulating double-glazed units
fichas.summary: Thermally insulating double glazing uses a precious-metal coating, commonly at position 3, to achieve low thermal conductivity. Inert-gas filling can improve insulation further. The units are intended to retain high visual and overall energy transmittance for passive solar gain; applying the coating at position 2 reduces overall energy transmission.

dimensions.ocr_raw: The low coefficients of thermal conductivity (Ug-value) are achieved through a coating of precious metal in position 3.

fichas.title: Solar control glass
fichas.summary: Solar control glass combines high visual transmittance with low overall energy transmittance, limiting passive solar gain. A thin precious-metal coating is protected in the cavity between panes. Units are labelled with visual and overall energy transmittance values, and are available in different colours and exterior reflection grades. The text advises checking manufacturer samples because exact colour matching and undistorted reflections cannot always be achieved.
